newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia late palm olein stable, trade dull.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia late palm olein stable, trade dull.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were generally stable in quiet late trading on Wednesday as buyers stuck to the sidelines waiting for lower values, traders said.
They said olein was around 1,400-10 in Jakarta and 1,375-80 rupiah in the North Sumatran city of Medan. November delivery olein was quoted at 1,380 rupiah in Jakarta.
"The market was very, very quiet," one trader said. "Buyers are standing back as the selling pressure mounts."
He said the suspension of October crude palm oil exports by the state-run joint marketing board (KPB) had caused fears of a possible oversupply in the local market.
Another attributed the weak market sentiment to President Suharto's recent call for market operations by the state logistics agency BULOG to control food prices.
Traders said the October palm oil export taxes announced officially by the government late on Tuesday could help olein exports due to a lowering in the tax.
The export tax on RBD palm olein was lowered to $30 per tonne in October from $47.60 in September. That on crude palm oil, however, was raised to $35.28 from $34.16 last month.
